biography.title: Biography
biography.p1: José Luis López Ruiz (Linares, Jaén, 1993) holds a B.Sc. in Computer Engineering (2018), an M.Sc. in Computer Engineering with the Best Master's Thesis Award (2020) and a Ph.D. in Information and Communication Technologies (2023), all from the University of Jaén. He currently serves as Assistant Professor (Profesor Ayudante Doctor) in the Department of Computer Science and is a member of the ASIA (TIC-257) research group at the same university. He has held the ANECA accreditation as Lecturer (Profesor Permanente Laboral) since December 2023. His research lines combine Internet of Things, fuzzy logic and deep learning in connected-health and active-ageing systems.
biography.p2: My academic career has developed entirely within the Department of Computer Science at the University of Jaén, where I started in 2019 as research staff under the Youth Guarantee programme. Between 2020 and 2022 I worked as an R&D&I Support and Management Technician in the ASIA research group and, in February 2022, I joined university teaching as a Substitute Lecturer, a position I held until 2024. In late 2024 I obtained an Assistant Professor (Profesor Ayudante Doctor) position in the Computer Architecture and Technology area. In 2025 I was awarded a José Castillejo grant for young doctors from the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities for a three-month research stay (May–July 2026) at Ulster University (Belfast, United Kingdom).
biography.p3: My research is currently organised in four complementary lines, all focused on intelligent systems applied to health and active ageing. The first one, started during my doctoral thesis, tackles the recognition of activities of daily living using IoT sensors deployed in domestic and care environments, aimed at monitoring older adults and chronic patients. A second line, derived from the first, addresses glucose monitoring and management of type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus, combining treatment-adherence platforms with the generation of linguistic summaries from sensor data through fuzzy logic and language models. In parallel I develop indoor positioning systems with BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) and UWB (ultra-wideband) technologies, applied mainly to assisted living, where they make it possible to detect multi-occupancy in monitored spaces without resorting to cameras. Finally, I have recently started a fourth line on stress detection from biometric data in low-cost IoMT (Internet of Medical Things) devices. Across these four lines, I maintain continuous work on efficient IoT/IoMT architectures and the assessment of their alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
